Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
Comments: Zambia Internet Exchange (Zambia IX) in Lusaka shows Active subnet with 13 participants; established Feb 2006 per Packet Clearing House listing.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited PCH record (Zambia IXP, est. 2006) is actually listed with status 'Unknown' and no active subnets — it does not support the claimed 13 participants. A separate, currently active exchange, LSK-IX (Lusaka IXP, managed by Infratel, est. 2023), is confirmed via PeeringDB (10 peers, 76G capacity) and Internet Society Pulse (members incl. MTN, Airtel, Zamtel, ZAMREN, Zambia Revenue Authority, Paratus, PCH). Code 4 (Active IXP with moderate participation) is confirmed on this corrected evidence, but the original source citation was inaccurate and should be replaced.

Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)
Comments: No major hyperscaler (AWS/Azure/Google) region indicated locally in evidence gathered; Cloudscene lists only a few hosting/cloud providers in Lusaka market (suggesting remote/regional reliance).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed by an independent, more recent source: Inflect (September 2025) states there are zero direct cloud on-ramps for AWS, Azure or GCP in Zambia, with Johannesburg the nearest hyperscale hub — consistent with the original Cloudscene-based assessment. Note for human review: Liquid C2/Boston IT market an 'Azure Stack' hybrid-cloud appliance hosted in Zambia since 2023, which could arguably support a higher score (edge node presence); this claim comes only from vendor/trade-press sources and Inflect's independent assessment does not treat it as a cloud on-ramp, so it was not used to upgrade the score.

Value Name: Comprehensive requirements for personal data or broad categories
Comments: Zambia Data Protection Act No.3 of 2021 requires controllers/processors to store and process personal and sensitive personal data on servers/data centres located in Zambia (Section 70(1)) with limited exceptions.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 (s.70) requirement to store personal/sensitive data on servers located in Zambia is corroborated by a July 2025 Xalam Analytics data-centre market brief, which independently notes the Act's localisation rules. Code 4 unchanged.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
Comments: Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 enacted; establishes Office of Data Protection Commissioner to register/licence and oversee compliance (implementation still developing).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and strengthened with fresher sources. The Data Protection Act 2021 established the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC); a Commissioner was appointed in June 2023 and the ODPC was declared 'fully operational' in April 2025, with a mandatory controller/processor registration deadline of 30 April 2025 and statutory penalties for non-compliance. Code 4 confirmed; flagged for human review as this maturing framework may soon warrant Code 5 once documented enforcement actions occur.

Definition: Frequency and severity of power outages experienced by businesses and households. Based on World Bank Enterprise Surveys, Afrobarometer, or national utility data. Reflects the quality of electricity supply beyond mere access — critical for running ICT equipment and data infrastructure.
Comments: MTF reports average outage duration 7.2 hours/month for grid-connected households; reliability issues noted though many in high tier.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The 2017 MTF-based figure (7.2 hours/month, Code 3) is badly outdated. Zambia suffered a severe El Nino-driven drought from 2024 that cut Kariba hydropower output to a fraction of capacity, forcing load-shedding of up to 21 hours/day (BBC, Sept 2024; ACAPS, Jan 2025) affecting over 80% of the population. As of May 2025, ZESCO was still rationing at around 7 hours/day. This is clearly 'severe/frequent daily outages' — code changed from 3 to 1.

An unofficial community-maintained repository claims around 1,240 GitHub users in Zambia, which would technically suggest 'Developing', but this is not an authoritative source.
